phases.name: Policy contracts and safe defaults
gates: When no policy is enabled, preserve R8 behavior
Literal bounded rules and explicit field semantics
Separate intentional exclusions from parse failures
Old clients cannot acknowledge unsupported policy bundles

phases.name: Runtime selective input and output field removal
gates: Filter logical records before parsing and customer storage
Three supplied records select exactly the EHLO raw record
Excluded input advances cursors without quarantine or endpoint delivery
Output fields removed after enrichment at final customer delivery
Consistent file, Loki, ClickHouse, replay and quarantine partial-JSON behavior
Atomic activation and rollback

phases.name: Revisioned control plane and recovery
gates: Draft preview cannot activate policy
Independent review and publish
Enable/disable and revoke restore pass-through appropriately
Exact client capability and hash acknowledgement
Both new asset classes in backup/restore without deleting existing definitions

phases.name: Two optional workspaces and AI guidance
gates: Load pasted/file samples
Run filter shows raw records first
Parse only on explicit action
Output before/after field removal preview
RBAC, reset, revision editing and status
Step-by-step verified AI navigation and bounded live Gemini test

phases.name: Qualification and stress
gates: One million selective-input records with exact accepted/excluded counts
One million output-removal records with exact kept fields
Mixed rules, disabled policies, malformed input, multiline, reload and failure scenarios
Full Linux, vet, meaningful race/fuzz and browser checks
Tab/subtab/control coverage inventory with honest limits
Actual packaged client/controller sync, restore and restart

phases.name: Local build and publication
gates: Two byte-identical builds
Fresh archive installer and checksum checks
R8-compatible installer modes and mixed-role preservation
Published bytes match verified local files

limits: Finite tests cannot prove every possible log, button state, network or hardware condition
Throughput is measured rather than promising one million records per second or zero latency
Intentionally excluded consumed records require original-source replay to recover
Output policy targets explicit customer JSON root fields; it does not delete internal audit/health records
